lesson.title: Comparing Quadratic Functions
intro: Quadratic functions can be compared by their minimum or maximum values.
A function written in equation form can often be analyzed by finding its vertex or axis of symmetry.
A graph can also be used to compare quadratic functions visually.
The axis of symmetry of a parabola is the vertical line through its vertex.

workedExample.problem: Find the axis of symmetry of \(h(x)=x^2-4x-5\).
workedExample.aiHint: For a quadratic in standard form, use \(x=\frac{-b}{2a}\).

questions.prompt: Four quadratic functions are represented below. Which function has the smallest minimum value?
questions.explanation: From the graph, function III has the lowest vertex, so it has the smallest minimum value.

questions.prompt: The axis of symmetry is \(x=2\) for which quadratic function?
questions.explanation: For \(h(x)=x^2-4x-5\), the axis of symmetry is \(x=\frac{-b}{2a}=\frac{-(-4)}{2(1)}=2\).
